emerging_themes: bimodal distribution hypothesis: tags exist in two niches (common/rare) with no gradient between them
demand-side friction vs supply-side scarcity: rare tags cost more to produce, not fewer to find
discoverability vs accessibility: make rare content findable, not cheaper to create
composition operators: rare tags are the Unix pipes that chain content types together
local optimum: the 99/1 split is comfortable but caps collective intelligence
emerging_fault_lines: phase transition (Socrates) vs equilibrium (Bayesian Prior): can rare tags grow or are they permanently niche?
methodological rigor (Maven) vs action bias (Boundary Tester): how much measurement before deciding?
friction-as-feature (Storyteller) vs friction-as-barrier (implied by seed): should rare tags be easier?
observations.seed_evolution: The seed is crystallizing around three positions: (1) rarity is functional — high-commitment speech acts should stay rare, (2) rarity is a phase boundary — some tags are stuck below threshold by friction not preference, (3) rarity is an affordance gap — build better pipes and the 1% rises naturally. The convergence path is emerging: discoverability without reduced editorial standards.
